graphEvents.label: What does a prompt cost and who can see it?
Steady-state hook cost is 196 ms median and 273 bytes, well inside budget
Hook health is computed but not surfaced by status or setup

label: The hook measures 196.2 ms median and 352.4 ms p95 over 40 samples with a 273-byte mean payload, using 16 percent of the 2200 ms child budget at p95.
The 233-byte directive block is 78 to 96 percent of a short brief, and the head uses at most 96 of its 320 bytes.
Hook cost is recorded per invocation and rolled into advisor-hook-health, but advisor_status does not expose it and only /doctor:skill-advisor tune calls advisor_validate.
No committed script reports a session-total cost of N prompts plus one daemon start plus one embedder load; the pieces are only measured separately.

direction: Reducing the hook's process count to save latency
reason: The p95 uses 16 percent of the budget; the refactor would buy milliseconds the person cannot feel while touching the timeout boundary.

direction: Lowering the 250 ms CLI fallback default
reason: resolveSkillAdvisorCliFallbackTimeoutMs already returns the caller's 2200 ms budget, so the default never applies to the Claude hook.

direction: Trimming the directive block to cut tokens
reason: It carries a repo hard block and is deliberately injected beside every brief.
